description: Wire the runtime into OverlayService and CloudControlClient with the minimum additive changes: OverlayService owns/initializes SceneRenderer + SceneRuntimeController, restores the active manifest, forwards scheduler events to the regie, selects Case A vs Case B deterministically, hides on eligibility loss, and cleans up on stop; CloudControlClient installs runtimeTrack+manifest atomically and only ACKs after full durable install + scheduler accept + regie accept. Also add the SceneRenderer scene-asset preflight so a missing asset fails bounded without a partial render. Includes a scene-asset preflight test and renderer-boundary coverage (sections 7, 8, 11, 15, 19, 20-A, 20-E). Depends on FEAT-002 and FEAT-003.
steps: Audit OverlayService.onStartCommand / onDestroy before editing. Add (do NOT rewrite): lazily create SceneRenderer (new SceneRenderer(this, assetResolver, this::onPermissionLost)) and a SceneRuntimeController, plus an AssetResolver implementation that resolves ONLY from the existing local asset seam and returns null when absent (NO network, NO download — section 15). Keep the foreground service, specialUse, lifecycle, boot/autostart, pairing, Cloud client, MediaSessionProbe, MediaIdentityMatcher, existing scheduler, and legacy OverlayRenderer all intact.

In the scheduler Listener inside OverlayService, add Case A vs Case B branching using the FEAT-003 predicate (valid manifest active for the current revision): Case A (no manifest) -> existing legacy path (showRenderer + OverlayRenderer.showTrackedCommentary) UNCHANGED; Case B (valid manifest) -> forward the due Event to SceneRuntimeController (which drives SceneRenderer) and do NOT call the legacy OverlayRenderer for that comment. onPlayback -> forward to whichever path is active. onEligibility(false) -> hide the active path immediately (legacy renderer.onTrackEligibility(false) OR controller.hideAll()), never both visible at once. Ensure exactly one visual path per comment.

On service start/boot-prepare, restore the active revision: load runtimeTrack into the scheduler (as today) AND, if that revision has a durable valid manifest, load it into the SceneRuntimeController (armed, not visible — nothing renders until an eligible due event). A no-manifest revision restores exactly as today (Case A).

In onDestroy / stop, dismiss SceneRenderer (dismissNow) and unload the controller in addition to existing cleanup; a render requested after stop must be ignored (covered by FEAT-003 guard + null-safe service state).

Update CloudControlClient.fetchAssignment ordering for ACK invariant (section 7): when the assignment carries an overlayManifest, parse it (OverlayManifestParser), run VideoOverlayManifestBridge cross-contract validation against the parsed runtimeTrack, and persist runtimeTrack+manifest atomically via the FEAT-002 repository BEFORE ACK. ACK (unchanged protocol: deviceId via path, revision, finalTrackId) only after: runtimeTrack valid + manifest valid + cross-contract valid + durably persisted + scheduler accepted/restored the track + regie accepted/restored the manifest. Any failure in that chain => NO ACK, keep the prior valid cache intact, set a bounded diagnostic (MANIFEST_INVALID/INCONSISTENT/CACHE_FAILED), never log comment/scene text or secrets. Keep the no-manifest (Case A) assignment path exactly as today. CloudControlClient must NOT contain the cross-contract rules themselves — it calls the bridge. Note: CloudControlClient has no direct regie reference today; thread the regie-accept step through the smallest seam (e.g. a callback/interface the service supplies, or the repository restore the service performs) rather than adding graphics logic to the client.

Add a SceneRenderer scene preflight (section 15): before mutating the overlay window for a Video scene, verify every image element's asset resolves locally; if any asset is missing, fail the scene in a bounded way (no crash, no partial render, bounded diagnostic SCENE_ASSET_UNAVAILABLE / SCENE_RENDER_FAILED) and do not leave a half-drawn window. Keep SceneRenderer network-free and keep dismiss idempotent.

Add JVM tests. Section 20-A (cases 1-3): an assignment without a manifest is still accepted and routed to the legacy path, and legacy behavior is unchanged (assert the Case A predicate chooses legacy and the regie is not engaged). Section 20-E renderer-boundary coverage that is feasible in pure JVM / with Android stubs: image-with-missing-asset => bounded failure, no crash (preflight returns failure); dismiss idempotent; zIndex ordering is deterministic (reuse SceneRenderer.ordered logic if extractable, otherwise test the controller/preflight boundary). For primitives that genuinely require an Android view (text/rectangle/group/table/image-with-asset/fade/coords), assert them via the existing parser fixtures + a thin preflight/boundary rather than instantiating real Views where the test runtime returns Android default stubs; document which 20-E cases are proven by unit test vs which remain CI/physical. Section 7/8 ordering: add a test (or extend an existing CloudControlClient-style async test) proving no ACK is emitted when manifest validation or atomic persistence fails, and ACK is emitted only after a full successful install (reuse the ManualExecutor pattern from CloudResetAsyncTest if touching the client, or test the install+ack-decision helper directly).
acceptance_criteria: OverlayService initializes/owns SceneRenderer + SceneRuntimeController, restores an active manifest armed-not-visible, forwards scheduler events, hides on eligibility loss, and cleans up on stop — without rewriting the service or altering the preserved subsystems.
Case A (no manifest) is byte-for-byte the legacy path; Case B (valid manifest) drives SceneRenderer via the regie; the two are never visible simultaneously for the same comment.

CloudControlClient ACKs a manifested revision ONLY after runtimeTrack+manifest+cross-contract valid + atomic durable persist + scheduler accept + regie accept; any failure => no ACK, prior cache intact, bounded diagnostic, no content/secret logged; ACK protocol fields unchanged; cross-contract rules live in the bridge, not the client.
SceneRenderer performs a scene-asset preflight: a missing asset yields a bounded scene failure with no crash and no partial render; SceneRenderer stays network-free; dismiss is idempotent.
Section 20-A (1-3) legacy tests pass; feasible 20-E renderer-boundary tests pass; an ACK-ordering test proves no premature ACK; all pre-existing tests still pass.
No change to applicationId/package/version/permissions/FGS/pairing/recovery/signing; no new permission; android-release.yml untouched.
findings:
Implemented additively, no rewrite of any preserved subsystem.

SceneRenderer: added a pure, Android-free scene-asset preflight. `preflight(Scene)` resolves every IMAGE assetRef (via the local AssetResolver only, never network) and returns false when any is missing; `render()` now calls preflight first so a missing asset never produces a partial window. Extracted `imageAssetRefs(Scene)` (static, recurses group children) and `orderedForTest(...)` so the asset-walk and z-order are unit-testable without real Views. dismiss stays idempotent, SceneRenderer stays network-free.

SceneRuntimeController: unchanged (FEAT-003 already exposes the SceneSink/preflight seam).

OverlayService: owns a lazily-created SceneRenderer + a SceneRuntimeController + a local-only AssetResolver (`resolveLocalAsset` returns null; the POC ships no asset transport). The scheduler Listener now branches Case A vs Case B via `isSceneRendererActive()` -> `controller.isSceneRendererActiveFor(activeRevision)`: Case A path (showRenderer + OverlayRenderer.showTrackedCommentary) is byte-for-byte unchanged; Case B forwards the due Event to the controller. onPlayback forwards to the active path; onEligibility always disarms the controller and hides the legacy renderer only when it owns the comment, so the two are never visible at once. On service start, restoreWithManifest re-arms a durable manifested revision armed-not-visible (loadManifest), else legacy restore() keeps Case A. onDestroy and ACTION_CLOUD_RESET unload the controller and dismissNow the SceneRenderer. Added a static Android-free `installManifestedRevision(...)` helper that is the ACK-decision core.

CloudControlClient: added a `ManifestInstaller` seam (supplied by OverlayService) and an overloaded production/test constructors. fetchAssignment now branches on `overlayManifest`: when present it calls the installer (atomic persist + bridge cross-contract + scheduler accept + regie accept) BEFORE the ACK and only ACKs on full success; any failure throws => NO ACK, prior cache intact, bounded diagnostic. The no-manifest (Case A) path is unchanged. ACK protocol fields (revision, finalTrackId; deviceId via path) are unchanged. The cross-contract rules remain in VideoOverlayManifestBridge, not the client.

Diagnostics: reused the FEAT-002 MANIFEST_* bounded codes (MANIFEST_INVALID/INCONSISTENT/CACHE_FAILED). A missing-asset preflight failure records MANIFEST_INCONSISTENT (repo-adapted bounded code) rather than introducing a new enum constant, to avoid touching the diagnostics enum/Python boundary in this feature (dedicated SCENE_ASSET_UNAVAILABLE/SCENE_RENDER_FAILED codes are a candidate for FEAT-005 with the Python-boundary extension). No content/secret is logged.

Tests added (12, all green): SceneRendererPreflightTest (5) proves the asset-walk incl. group children, text-only no-asset, null-safe, and deterministic z-order; ManifestInstallAckDecisionTest (7) proves section 7 ACK ordering via the installManifestedRevision helper (coherent => ACK-able + regie armed; inconsistent/invalid/non-durable => NOT ACK-able + prior cache intact + bounded diagnostic) and section 20-A cases 1-3 (no-manifest legacy install, Case A predicate chooses legacy with regie not engaged, manifested restore refuses a non-manifested revision without clearing).

20-E coverage split: unit-proven in pure JVM = image-with-missing-asset bounded failure (preflight collector + controller suppression in SceneRuntimeControllerTest.preflightFailureSuppressesShow), dismiss idempotent (controller SceneSink contract), deterministic zIndex ordering. Remaining CI/physical (require a real Android View under returnDefaultValues stubs) = actual pixel rendering of text/rectangle/group/table/image-with-asset, fade enter/exit timing, and logical->physical coordinate scaling; these are proven here only up to the parser contract (that they parse into the expected primitives) and the pure preflight/ordering seam.

Gates all green: python3 -m unittest discover -s tests (13); gradle8.9 :app:testDebugUnitTest :app:lintDebug :app:assembleDebug; SCENEVIBE_ENABLE_LAN_DEV=true assembleDebug; SCENEVIBE_CLOUD_ORIGIN=... assembleDebug. No change to applicationId/package/version/permissions/FGS/pairing/recovery/signing; no new permission; workflows untouched. An Android emulator/device is not available in the sandbox, so the api35 smoke and physical Sony BRAVIA qualifications remain CI/human-only and are NOT claimed here.
